title: Freeze Distribution Alpha scope and task graph
purpose: Start the Distribution Alpha workflow from the completed runtime foundation and decompose the next distribution-grade TASK chain.
scope: Create the Distribution Alpha workflow directory.
Create plan.json, context.md, task plan documentation, and TASK-DALPHA task JSON files.
Mark MVP skeleton-only promotion as out of scope.
Carry forward runtime, safety, release, and QEMU gates.
Identify the next executable task as the rootfs runtime artifact install manifest.
acceptance_criteria: Distribution Alpha plan includes the six required task areas from the runtime foundation entry criteria.
Plan explicitly depends on Runtime Foundation final audit.
Firecracker is represented as an Alpha executor profile behind SecurityExecutionEngine.
Only planning artifacts and task index/state files are touched.
verification: Parse all new workflow JSON files.
Review TASK.md current workflow and next-step section.
Run git status --short and confirm no Rust WIP is staged.
risk_notes: If this task is vague, later image work can regress into boot-only artifact promotion.
implementation_steps: Create the Distribution Alpha workflow session.
Create plan.json with waves, task graph, inherited gates, and confidence score.
Create one TASK-DALPHA JSON per planned task.
Create human-readable Alpha task plan documentation.
Update TASK.md and .workflow/state.json to point to the new active workflow.
failure_modes: Plan omits runtime state, policy/tool/model config, service recovery smoke, QEMU runtime smoke, or release provenance gates.
Plan allows Alpha promotion from the MVP boot skeleton alone.
Plan makes Firecracker a parallel side-effect path.
Planning commit stages unrelated Rust WIP.

verification_matrix.expected: All workflow, plan, task, and evidence JSON files parse
Required entry-criteria task areas are represented
Only Alpha planning files plus TASK.md/.workflow/state.json are staged for this commit

blocked_until: TASK.md and .workflow/state.json point to the Alpha workflow.
